nodes.name: Totora reed
nodes.desc: A tall sedge growing in shallow water, mainly less than 3 m deep. Its reed belt is breeding habitat for the Titicaca grebe, and the Uru people build their floating islands from it.

nodes.name: Stoneworts and pondweeds
nodes.desc: Underwater plants and algae that carpet the lake bed below the reeds. Slate-colored coots feed on them, especially Chara.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton and algae
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae in the open water and on the lake bottom. They feed the lake's small grazers and filter feeders.

nodes.name: Ichu bunchgrass
nodes.desc: A tussock grass common on the altiplano slopes and rocky shores around the lake.

nodes.name: Hyalella amphipods
nodes.desc: Small freshwater crustaceans, many endemic to the lake. They are a main food of the Titicaca water frog.

nodes.name: Heleobia snails
nodes.desc: Tiny freshwater snails, many found only in the lake. They graze on the lake bottom and are eaten by frogs and fish.

nodes.name: Slate-colored coot
nodes.desc: A waterbird that eats mostly aquatic plants, with Chara a main part of its diet. It nests among reeds or on floating vegetation.

nodes.name: Chilean flamingo
nodes.desc: Filter-feeds in shallow water on algae, plankton and small invertebrates, stirring up sediment with its feet.

nodes.name: Southern viscacha
nodes.desc: A rock-dwelling rodent of the Andes that eats grasses, moss and lichens. The Andean mountain cat preys on it.

nodes.name: Orestias killifish
nodes.desc: A genus of pupfish, most of it endemic to Titicaca. Species eat crustaceans, snails, algae, plankton and other fish. Introduced trout and pollution threaten it.

nodes.name: Titicaca water frog
nodes.desc: A fully aquatic frog that eats mainly amphipods and snails, and adults also take Orestias fish. Overcollection, pollution and trout have cut its numbers.

nodes.name: Andean gull
nodes.desc: An opportunistic feeder at highland lakes, taking insects, amphibians, small fish and sometimes waterbird eggs and chicks.

nodes.name: Puna ibis
nodes.desc: Probes shallow water and mud for invertebrates, and takes amphibians and small fish when it can. It nests in tall wetland vegetation.

nodes.name: Rainbow trout
nodes.desc: An introduced predator. Wikipedia attributes the likely extinction of one Orestias species to competition and predation by introduced trout and silverside.

nodes.name: Titicaca grebe
nodes.desc: A flightless, endangered grebe. Nearly 95% of its prey mass is Orestias. It breeds in the reed belt and drowns in gill nets.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong high-altitude light, at about 3,800 m, reaches the shallow lake and drives its plant growth.

nodes.name: Lake water
nodes.desc: Cool, clear freshwater at high altitude with oxygen that is limited by elevation. Reeds and underwater plants grow in its shallows.

nodes.name: Nutrients and runoff
nodes.desc: Nutrients from soil and wastes feed algae and plants. Sewage and mining waste from growing towns also pollute parts of the lake.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Microbes that break down dead reeds, plants and animals and return nutrients to the water.
